title: Send personal note to Neil Jenkins about draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 (drafted, not sent)
description:
Personal note to Neil Jenkins (RFC 8620 co-author with Chris Newman; JMAP Calendars and Contacts editor) about draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00. Drafted 2026-11-15. NOT SENT; needs Mark's explicit approval. Send AFTER the list email (jmap-chat-spec-0577), and replace LIST-THREAD-URL with the mailarchive link to it.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
From: Mark Atwood <mark@reviewcommit.com>
To: Neil Jenkins <neilj@fastmailteam.com>
Subject: draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 touches RFC 8620 and JMAP Calendars

Hi Neil,

A short heads-up, since you'll know best whether this is the right
shape. I posted draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00 to jmap@ today:

https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/jmap/Orpk4MzWlbrwBPVSa5cVQ5_vt0s/

When Éric Vyncke asked about single-language name and description on
the sharing draft, you said multi-language versions "could of course be
added by a future document"; this is my attempt at that document. It
updates RFC 8620 and touches Calendars and Contacts:

- It builds on 8620 3.8 and doesn't replace it. A new optional
  capability adds JSCalendar-style locale and localizations to
  Calendar and AddressBook name and description, plus a language
  argument on /get, /query and /queryChanges. CalendarEvent and
  ContactCard are left to JSCalendar and JSContact.
- For clients that opt in, Accept-Language never changes /get data
  for these properties, so a client's state-keyed cache can't mix
  languages.
- It leaves out ParticipantIdentity: the name is the sender's own, so
  it shouldn't follow the reader's language.
- For all of JMAP, at SHOULD level: 7807 becomes 9457, problem details
  come from every HTTP resource (Session, event source, WebSocket
  handshake), URI-valued properties follow RFC 3986, and there are
  text-handling rules.

My main question for you: would you rather see the SHOULD-level parts
go into an 8620bis instead of a separate Updates document? I'm happy
to reshape it either way.

Thanks,
Mark
